name: Slider
description: An input where the user selects a value from within a given range by moving a thumb along a bar or track.

required_attributes.description: Current value. On <input type='range'> the browser derives it — do not set it yourself.

optional_attributes.description: Human-readable string when numeric value is not intuitive
vertical for vertical sliders; default is horizontal
Use when the number alone is not meaningful: aria-valuenow='2' aria-valuetext='Medium'. Screen readers announce this INSTEAD of valuenow.
Default horizontal. For a vertical range input, prefer CSS writing-mode over the attribute.

notes: Use <input type='range'>. It gives you arrows, Home/End, Page Up/Down, the value announcement, the form value, and — critically — click-anywhere-on-the-track, which is what satisfies RAWeb 13.10.2.
RAWeb 13.10 test 2: a drag is a path-based gesture. Tapping a point on the track must set the value too. This is free with <input type='range'> and is the thing custom sliders forget.
A range input cannot be labelled by its own value — it needs a <label for>. The visible value is a separate element (RAWeb 11.1).
aria-valuetext replaces the announced number entirely. Use it for non-numeric scales (Low/Medium/High) or units ('€250', '3 stars').

Vertical sliders: use CSS `writing-mode: vertical-rl` (or `appearance: slider-vertical` in older engines) rather than a rotate() transform — a rotated slider keeps horizontal arrow-key semantics, which then contradict the visual.
Never put tabindex on the track — only the thumb is focusable. With <input type='range'> the input IS the thumb.
The value must commit on pointer UP, not down (RAWeb 13.11), so the user can drag away to abort.

raweb_criteria.reason: The current value must be exposed via aria-valuenow, and aria-valuetext where the raw number is not meaningful.
Arrow keys, Home/End and Page Up/Down must all adjust the value.
A slider sets a form value and needs a real associated label.
The thumb must show a visible focus indicator.
Test 13.10.2 — dragging a thumb is a PATH-BASED gesture. The same value must be settable with a single-point operation (tapping the track). A drag-only slider fails.
The value must commit on pointer release, and dragging away must be abortable.
